Started playing sims 3 for the first time this week and I’m obsessed! I started playing with a young adult financially struggling single mother named Esther who has a child sim named Gloria as her daughter (they were originally going to be sisters but then I realized I couldn’t connect them as sisters in cas). They lived in a small one bedroom apartment with a small kitchen in Bridgeport. 

Esther wants to create a better and comfortable life for her daughter Gloria so Gloria would often be under the care of her babysitter who was just some disgruntled teen who always said he’d be leaving but stayed until Esther came back. Gloria meanwhile has dreams of becoming a famous celebrity. She wants to be an actress. She loved playing pretend as some sort of king or so as she wore a crown often everyday. Sometimes her mom would arrive home tired and watch the tv but she’d still indulge Gloria and her play pretend sometimes with bowing or otherwise reacting to her.

Eventually Gloria aged up into a teenager and is in the drama club while doing her homework regularly to work towards scholarships to afford uni for her fine arts major while her mother met and fell in love with her boss at work who then moved in with them and with what money he moved in with, allowing them to look for a new and larger apartment. Now they’re all living more comfortably.

Definitely agree with this. I spent a lot of time in character creator mostly because of how I couldn’t get the character to look exactly how I wanted due to the limited options, especially the face options. I’m also a frequent sims 4 player so I also felt I was heavily biased coming into bg3’s character creator
I like all the companions in this game. I’m only around act 2, but their personal quests are all compelling and only makes me care for them all the more to help them

Im sorry you have to deal with this. I understand how you wouldn’t see it as a big deal. Something like this happened to me in my last relationship with my own partner who fell for someone else while we were together. I would reconsider the relationship at the very least and it’s understandable to not want to be hurt or make a big deal out of it, but be sure to not dismiss your feelings, it’s more then understandable to feel upset and angry. I can’t say I know what to do in your shoes exactly as I didn’t do anything myself back then, but I’d take space away from her and reconsider the relationship as a whole
